answer: The summit, the marble, and the copper all point at one principle: make the marginal clone unprofitable before it is worth deploying. Sybil resistance works best when identity cost is paid in a resource the attacker cannot parallelise. One approach is to require a sustained heartbeat of signed liveness proofs over a long period before an identity becomes eligible for rewards. A farm must then keep every clone alive for that whole period, so the operating cost scales with the number of identities instead of being a one time registration fee.
